import-rules-check.desc: Checks that a file's imports only point: - Sideways (to siblings in its own module); or - Deeper (into nested modules) And that they never point (violations): - Up to a parent module, unless to a commons module (see commons-modules below); or - Across into a different branch of the tree.

rule.desc: Sideways/deeper imports must be written with `super::` (never `crate::`).
rule.rationale: A single `super` resolves to the containing module and appending segments only goes deeper. So, a `super::`-rooted path can only ever point sideways or deeper.

rule.desc: Imports to a commons parent module must be written with `crate::` (never `super::super..`).
rule.rationale: To distinguish them from sideways/deeper imports

commons-modules.desc: c, t, s, ext_traits — shared-code (general shared logic, types, static data, and extension traits, respectively). Each may be a folder (`t/`) with a mod.rs file, or a single-file module (`t.rs`). All four behave the same way (e.g. `crate::c` is the whole-crate commons shared logic, reachable everywhere; `crate::app::c` is app-local, reachable only from files at or below `crate::app`). Additionally, inside a commons folder, the import-rules apply as if that folder were the crate root.
commons-modules.rationale: Need a way to share certain items. So, a shared item lives in a commons module at some level above everything using it.

config.item: ignore_export_macros - when true, imports of `#[macro_export]` macros are exempt (default false)
